content.text: Implement for 3.4 by introducing the templating mechanism, then implement on a piecemeal basis as code is touched by other fixes etc (not in 3.4)

Remove from 3.4 Milestone 4, this is an ongoing task (we should add it to new releases as they occur to highlight this, potentially could have a full review of all code at some point, but this would be quite a major task).

Just noting for future that one of the places where this would be really nice to have is with the REST API DefaultSerializer and the Access & Management package servlets that return API responses. Not to mention that there's significant duplication of code there too.
Has a templating library been chosen for this task?
stringtemplate is in use in some of the integration tests - but I'm not sure if it has made it into any  of the core code.

During discussion at the OR2011 Austin committers' meeting, I was wont to make the point that this is an issue that can be worked on without too much in-depth knowledge of the Fedora codebase, which might enable more developers to attack it. If that's an attractive proposition, then two qualities that should be paramount in deciding on a templating engine would be widespread knowledge and ease-of-use. Perhaps it would be worth committing to a single very popular engine so that as many developers as possible could work on this issue…
Retaking this issue as a way of getting to know the codebase again.
We should decide on the template engine. The most widespread engines seem to be:
Freemarker and Velocity seem to me to similar enough that the choice isn't too dangerous. I don't know enough about Stringtemplate to comment.

There are a number of occurrences where xml or html documents/fragements are embedded within the code. This has an impact on maintainability,readability,testability and separation of concerns. Most documents could easily be factored out by using a template engine, such as StringTemplate (

Remove from 3.4 Milestone 4, this is an ongoing task (we should add it to new releases as they occur to highlight this, potentially could have a full review of all code at some point, but this would be quite a major task).
